alignments.note: The neuter article of the adverbial idiom Τὸ λοιπόν has no separate English realization (rule 23). The ASV supplies it no nominal, unlike the τὰ of τὰ αὐτά below, so nothing is left for it to take.
Anarthrous ἐν κυρίῳ; the supplied determiner is a rule 7 helper on the noun, no article competing (rule 51).
No conjunction governs the clause, so the infinitival marker is the verb's own helper (rules 7, 40).

The article takes the determiner it was already given together with the supplied generic noun that completes its phrase, discontinuously across the pronoun's own word (rules 15, 102, 103), and heads on the nominal as rule 102 requires. τὰ ἐπίγεια → *earthly things* at 3:19 and τὰ πάντα → *all things* at 3:21 are the same shape. Giving *things* to αὐτά under rule 17's generic-noun clause remains defensible, but that clause is scoped to anarthrous Greek and an article stands here.
The identity pronoun keeps only its own word. Rule 60 refuses to read αὐτός as a demonstrative, so rule 49 does not empty the governing article.
The ASV writes a word for μέν, so it is aligned to it (rule 70).
The supplied copula of the verbless clause rides with the predicate adjective (rule 53), as throughout this chapter.
The clause expresses no subject, so the predicate adjective carries the supplied subject and copula (rule 68).

review_notes: Only the placement of t012 *things* and the head of the article unit change; the article keeps the *the* it already had.
Rule 60 refuses to read αὐτός as a demonstrative, so rule 49 does not empty the article here, and the pronoun keeps a bare *same* as the corpus gives it in its *same* units.
Τὸ λοιπόν stays `unrepresented`: the ASV writes one word, *Finally*, and supplies the article no nominal — which is the contrast that shows the article takes only what was written.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'as touching zeal' renders the noun alone; the variation is only between the neuter accusative ζῆλος and the masculine accusative ζῆλον of the same word, which no English wording can distinguish. No ASV note is mapped here.

alignments.note: Anarthrous quantifier: no article competes, so the supplied generic noun stays with it and the head is the quantifier (rule 17). Contrast τὰ πάντα below in this same verse.
The case preposition rides with the article's determiner (rule 21).
The determiner slot is occupied by the possessive of μου, so the article realizes nothing (rule 20).

The article takes the supplied generic noun completing its phrase and heads on it (rules 102, 103); rule 17 states this phrase in terms — τὰ πάντα → *all things* is the article's *things* and the quantifier's *all*. This corrects an `unrepresented` article, and matches τὰ πάντα at 3:21 and τὰ ἐπίγεια at 3:19. Leaving the article empty and giving *all things* whole to πάντα is the reading rule 17 names as the error, and the anarthrous πάντα earlier in this verse is where that reading belongs.
The quantifier keeps its own bare word, the supplied noun belonging to the article that governs it (rule 102).

The ASV builds a support-verb frame whose own supplied noun licenses the *of*, so the preposition stays inside the verb's unit and the governed phrase keeps a bare noun; the head is the meaning-bearing complement (rules 17, 21).
The supplied object pronoun is a rule 7 helper on the verb that requires it.

review_notes: Only s020 and s021 change; the article moves from `unrepresented` to `aligned` on *things*, and πάντα keeps a bare *all*.

The anarthrous πάντα at s005 is untouched and keeps *all things* whole headed on *All*: rule 17's generic-noun clause is scoped to anarthrous Greek, and this verse writes both shapes, which is what shows the article and not the English decides.

ἐζημιώθην keeps *I suffered the loss of* whole: the supplied frame noun *loss* is what licenses the *of*, so the preposition stays inside the verb's unit and the governed phrase keeps a bare noun (rule 21).

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'Yea verily, and I count' is an emphatic particle rendering that suits either μενοῦνγε or μέν οὖν; the intensive γε has no separate English exponent here, and no note is mapped to this unit.

ASV 'do count them but refuse' leaves the copula unexpressed, which is the ordinary English for ἡγοῦμαι with a predicate accusative whether or not εἶναι stands in the text; the earlier 'to be loss' renders a different clause and does not settle this one.

The variation is the Greek article on κοινωνίαν and on τῶν παθημάτων; ASV 'the fellowship of his sufferings' requires the English definite article regardless, so the wording distinguishes nothing. No note is mapped here.
συμμορφιζόμενος and συμμορφούμενος are alternative present passive participles of the same verb with identical sense; ASV 'becoming conformed unto his death' renders either.
ASV 'the resurrection from the dead' carries an explicit prepositional phrase answering ἐκ νεκρῶν; the RP reading τῶν νεκρῶν is a bare genitive that ASV renders 'of the dead', not 'from the dead'.

alignments.note: ASV renders the conditional periphrastically; 'so be that' is licensed by ei, not by kai. Reading ei kai as a fixed concessive pair over one English idiom stays defensible.
Adverbial kai (glossed 'also', as at s015) has no English word here; the ASV renders it nowhere. It could instead be read as part of a fixed ei kai.

The ASV's underlying text reads Ἰησοῦ after Χριστοῦ, a name the projected base text omits (textual unit SBLGNT.PHP.3.12.v007). The unit is underdetermined: 'by Christ Jesus' excludes the bare Χριστοῦ of r00-base, but r01 (Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ) and r02 (τοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ) both remain, so the projection carries the r00-base fallback and no source token in this verse answers to 'Jesus' (rules 5, 12). This is not rule 7: 'Jesus' is a second name, not a helper on s018, which has its own 'Christ' at t035; and not rule 37, since no neighbouring verse holds the licensing token.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'laid hold on by Christ Jesus' names both Christ and Jesus, which excludes the bare Χριστοῦ of r00-base; the article of r02 has no English exponent, so r01 and r02 both remain. The mapped note is an alternative_rendering about the verb and does not bear on the name.

ASV reads 'I count not myself yet to have laid hold', and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities omit yet' reports that word as the disputed one — so the ASV text carried οὔπω and the omission is the noted alternative.

ASV 'unto the prize' renders either εἰς or ἐπί with the accusative of goal; English 'unto' does not separate them. The mapped note 'Or, upward' is an alternative_rendering touching ἄνω κλήσεως, not this unit.

alignments.note: Preposition and relative pronoun fused into the portmanteau *whereunto* (rule 35).

The case preposition and the supplied demonstrative determiner ride with the article (rules 21, 60), and the supplied nominal completing the elliptical phrase is the article's too, headed on it (rules 102, 103; rule 60's closing clause, τῆς μελλούσης → *that hour which* heading on *hour*). The unit is discontinuous across the pronoun's own word (rule 15). This is not rule 97's excluded-reading case: the ASV's own text lacked κανόνι, which is why the word is italicized, and the selected reading SBLGNT.PHP.3.16.v010 r00-base agrees with it; rule 11 makes the italics evidence rather than a verdict. Marking *rule* `added` under rule 5 remains defensible, but rule 103 folds a supplied nominal standing inside a phrase a Greek article governs.
The identity pronoun keeps its own bare word, as at 3:1 (rules 60, 102).
Imperatival infinitive rendered as *let us walk*; the supplied subject and auxiliary are rule 7 and rule 9 helpers on the verb.

review_notes: The `added` unit is removed and its target joins the article's unit, whose head moves from the determiner to the supplied nominal (rule 102).

This is not rule 97: the ASV italicizes *rule* because the ASV's own text lacked κανόνι, and SBLGNT.PHP.3.16.v010 selected r00-base, which agrees with it, so no reading the ASV translated has been excluded.
αὐτῷ keeps a bare *same*, as at 3:1, and the case preposition still rides with the article's determiner (rule 21).

variant_decisions.evidence: The RP addition ends with a second infinitive clause τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν, 'to mind the same thing', and ASV 3:16 has no such clause: it stops at 'by that same rule let us walk'. The English noun 'rule' is a supplied complement for the bare τῷ αὐτῷ, not a witness to κανόνι.

alignments.note: Adverbial καί realized as *even*; the ASV writes a word for it (rule 65).
The article keeps only the determiner the ASV wrote for it; the supplied relativizer and copula go to the predicate noun (rules 92, 96).

The ASV expands the accusative appositive into a finite clause. The clause expresses no subject, so the predicate noun carries the supplied subject pronoun and copula (rules 63, 68, 96 — ἀπόστολοι → *they are the messengers* is the shape), and the supplied complementizer belongs to the expanded complement rather than to the governing λέγω (rule 85). The unit is discontinuous across the article's own *the* (rules 15, 92). σύμμορφον → *that it may be conformed* at 3:21 is the same frame. Marking *that they are* `added` under rules 5 and 62 remains defensible — *they* resumes tokens already spent — but rule 62 says in terms that rules 68 and 96 are untouched wherever a standing token is what the supplied verb predicates of, and ἐχθρούς is that token.
The case preposition rides with the article's determiner (rule 21).
Article before a name with no English determiner (rule 23).
The ASV writes no determiner, so the case preposition stays with the noun (rules 21, 23).

review_notes: The `added` unit is removed and its three targets join ἐχθρούς, discontinuously across the article's own *the* (rule 15).
The article is untouched and keeps only the determiner the ASV wrote for it (rules 92, 96).
σύμμορφον → *that it may be conformed* at 3:21 is the same frame folded the same way, which is what makes this a chapter split rather than two constructions.

alignments.note: Article displaced by genitive relative pronoun whose (rule 20).
Supplied copula of a verbless clause rides with the predicate, as at s009 and s013 and throughout the chapter.
Article displaced by genitive relative pronoun whose (rule 20).
Supplied copula of a verbless clause rides with the predicate; the intervening 'the' stays on its own article s008 (rule 15).
Article realized as possessive relative whose without explicit genitive pronoun (rule 20).
Supplied copula of a verbless clause rides with the predicate, which here is the prepositional phrase.
Article displaced by genitive pronoun autōn (rule 20).
Substantival article before participle realized as relative pronoun who (rule 32).
Substantivizing article realized as things (rule 22).
Substantival article takes the generic noun it licenses; an anarthrous panta could carry all things whole, but with the article present the pair splits.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'that it may be conformed to the body of his glory' expands a predicative σύμμορφον into a result clause, which translators do whether or not εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτό stands in the text; the clause therefore does not attest the longer reading.

αὑτῷ, αὐτῷ and ἑαυτῷ differ only in accentuation and contraction of the same third-person reference; ASV 'unto himself' is the natural rendering of all three, since an editor's unaspirated αὐτῷ here is still read reflexively.
